What is MLX?
MLX is Apple's array framework for running machine learning on Apple silicon. It uses unified memory so models can move between CPU and GPU without copying.

What does LoRA stand for?
LoRA stands for Low-Rank Adaptation. It freezes the base model and trains small low-rank matrices instead of all weights.

What is a quantized model?
A quantized model stores weights in fewer bits, such as 4-bit instead of 16-bit. It uses much less memory with a small loss in quality.

What is a learning rate?
The learning rate controls how much weights are updated per training step. Too high and training diverges; too low and it crawls.

Explain overfitting.
Overfitting is when a model memorizes training data and fails on new data. Regularization, more data, or stopping early helps.

What is an epoch in training?
An epoch is one full pass over the training dataset. Iteration or step is one optimizer update, which usually sees only a batch.

What is a token?
A token is a chunk of text a model reads, like a word or subword. Models split text into tokens with a tokenizer before training.

What is a transformer?
A transformer is a neural network built on attention, letting every token consider every other token. It powers most modern language models.

What does SLM mean?
SLM means small language model, typically under a few billion parameters. They run fast on-device and fine-tune cheaply.

What is gradient checkpointing?
Gradient checkpointing trades compute for memory by discarding activations and recomputing them during backprop. It reduces RAM use at the cost of speed.

What is a validation set?
A validation set is data held out from training to monitor generalization. It guides choices like when to stop and which checkpoint to keep.

What is perplexity?
Perplexity measures how surprised a model is by a text; lower is better. It roughly reflects the average branching factor per token.

What is a chat template?
A chat template formats messages with role markers like turn and end tokens. Training and inference must use the same template to match the model's expectations.

What is warmup in training?
Warmup raises the learning rate slowly over the first steps. It stabilizes early training and avoids large noisy updates at the start.

What is an adapter?
An adapter is a small set of extra weights trained on top of a frozen base model. At inference it can be merged into the base weights.

What does fine-tuning mean?
Fine-tuning continues training a pretrained model on a narrower dataset for a specific task. It adapts general knowledge to your data.

What is batch size?
Batch size is the number of examples processed before one weight update. Larger batches smooth gradients but need more memory.

What is unified memory?
Unified memory is one memory pool shared by the CPU and GPU on Apple silicon. Data can be used by both without copying between them.

What is a goroutine?
A goroutine is a lightweight thread managed by the Go runtime. Tens of thousands run concurrently because each starts with a small stack that grows on demand.

What is a Go channel?
A channel is a typed conduit for sending values between goroutines. It synchronizes communication so you usually don't need explicit locks.

What does defer do in Go?
defer schedules a function call to run when the surrounding function returns. Defers run last-in-first-out, after return values are set.

What is a Go interface?
An interface is a set of method signatures that a type implements implicitly. Go favors small interfaces over large class hierarchies.

What is context cancellation?
A context carries deadlines and cancellation signals across API boundaries. Callers cancel it to stop work that is no longer needed.

What is a Kafka topic?
A topic is a named stream of records partitioned across a cluster. Producers append records while consumers read them at their own pace.

What is consumer lag?
Consumer lag is the number of messages a consumer group has not yet processed. Growing lag means consumers can't keep up with producers.

Where does Kafka guarantee ordering?
Ordering is guaranteed only within a partition, not across a topic. Use a partition key when the order of related records matters.

What is an idempotent producer?
An idempotent producer retries safely without duplicating records after broker failures. It keeps at-least-once delivery from producing double writes.

What is gRPC?
gRPC is a high-performance RPC framework using HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers. It supports streaming and generates typed clients from a service definition.

What is a protocol buffer?
A protocol buffer is a compact binary serialization format defined in .proto files. Schemas evolve compatibly when new fields get fresh field numbers.

What is bidirectional streaming in gRPC?
Both client and server can send message streams independently over one HTTP/2 connection. Each side controls when it flushes and finishes.

How does gRPC handle deadlines?
Deadlines propagate through calls as timeouts on the context. Servers should check them and abort work that can no longer finish in time.

What is a Kubernetes Deployment?
A Deployment manages ReplicaSets to declaratively roll out and scale pods. It keeps the desired number of pods running during updates.

What is a liveness probe?
A liveness probe tells Kubernetes when to restart an unresponsive container. It should check process health, not downstream dependencies.

What is a readiness probe?
A readiness probe decides when a pod may receive traffic. Failing readiness removes the pod from Service endpoints without restarting it.

What is a Kubernetes Service?
A Service gives pods a stable virtual IP and DNS name for discovery. It load-balances across healthy pod endpoints.

What does desired versus ready mean in Kubernetes?
Desired is how many pod replicas the spec asks for; ready is how many currently pass readiness. A rollout stalls when ready never reaches desired.

What is a database index?
An index is an auxiliary structure that speeds reads on indexed columns. It costs extra space and slows writes on that table.

What is a covering index?
A covering index contains every column a query needs, so it answers from the index alone. The database avoids reading the table rows entirely.

What is a SQL join?
A join combines rows from tables using a condition, usually equality on keys. The query planner picks the join order and access method.

What is an EXPLAIN plan?
An EXPLAIN plan shows how the database will execute a query: access paths, join order, and estimated cost. It is the first tool for slow-query work.

What is a database transaction?
A transaction groups operations so they all succeed or all roll back. ACID semantics make concurrent failures behave predictably.

What is a cache hit ratio?
Cache hit ratio is the share of requests served from cache rather than the origin. Small improvements there can cut backend load dramatically.

What is cache invalidation?
Cache invalidation is removing or updating stale entries after data changes. It is hard because writers and caches disagree about time.

What is the thundering herd problem?
Thundering herd happens when many requests miss together and hit the backend at once. Request coalescing lets one caller fetch while others wait.

What is a write-through cache?
Write-through updates the cache and database together before acknowledging. It keeps reads fresh at the cost of slower writes.

What is a deadlock?
A deadlock occurs when goroutines wait on each other forever, each holding a resource the other needs. Consistent lock ordering prevents it.

What is lock contention?
Lock contention is time spent waiting because other threads hold the same lock. Sharding locks or lock-free structures reduces it.

What is backpressure?
Backpressure signals a fast producer to slow down when consumers fall behind. It keeps queues bounded instead of growing until failure.

What is graceful shutdown?
Graceful shutdown stops accepting new work, finishes in-flight requests, then exits. It prevents dropped requests during deploys.

What is the difference between metrics and logs?
Metrics are numeric time series for aggregation and alerting; logs are discrete event records for diagnosis. Use metrics to detect, logs to explain.

What is p99 latency?
p99 latency is the value that 99 percent of requests finish under. The worst one percent dominates user complaints, so averages hide real pain.

What is distributed tracing?
Distributed tracing follows one request across services using propagated context. Spans record timing so you can see where time is spent.

What is the difference between an SLI, an SLO and an SLA?
An SLI is a measured indicator, an SLO is the target for it, and an SLA is the contractual consequence of missing it. Teams set SLOs tighter than SLAs.

What is a flaky test?
A flaky test passes and fails on identical code, usually from timing, ordering, or shared state. Quarantine it and fix the root cause before trusting CI.

What is contract testing?
Contract testing verifies that provider and consumer agree on request and response shapes. It catches breaking API changes without full end-to-end environments.

What does DRY mean?
DRY means every piece of knowledge has one authoritative representation. It is about duplication of knowledge, not just copy-pasted lines.

What is an idempotency key?
An idempotency key lets a client retry a request safely because the server replays the first result. It makes at-least-once delivery feel exactly-once.

What is a bounded queue?
A bounded queue has a fixed capacity and applies backpressure when full. Unbounded queues trade short-term simplicity for eventual memory exhaustion.

What is eventual consistency?
Eventual consistency means replicas converge once writes stop propagating. Reads may be stale for a window, so systems expose that window explicitly.

What is the CAP theorem?
CAP says that during a network partition a system must choose between consistency and availability. Partitions are unavoidable, so that is the real trade.
